2026-11-06.headline: New SAF mappings connect Zero Trust objectives to roles and capabilities
2026-11-06.overview: A new Security standards and frameworks page maps framework objectives to SAF disciplines, roles, Microsoft security capabilities, and implementation guidance, including Zero Trust, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and the DoD Zero Trust Strategy. The SAF guidance now explains relationships among business priorities, risk, Zero Trust principles, disciplines, technologies, and technical solutions, while adding shared-responsibility, implementation, measurement, and four-component framework guidance. SAF navigation also shifts to objective- and role-based entry points. Most remaining updates refresh publication dates, internal references, or headings across Security Adoption and Zero Trust workshop pages.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Security architects and administrators can use the new mappings to plan improvements, coordinate responsibilities, and assess alignment with framework objectives. The revised SAF structure and navigation provide a clearer way to direct stakeholders to strategy, architecture, disciplines, scenarios, technologies, workshops, and related guidance. No configuration or migration action is indicated.
